title: Inquest into police custody death begins
article: A public inquest into the death of a 57-year old man in a Saskatoon police holding cell last year is scheduled to begin Monday.
Douglas Morissette was arrested around 7:15 p.m. on Jan. 15, 2013 for public intoxication. He also had outstanding summary offence warrants and was taken to detention.
Police have said he was assessed by an on-duty paramedic and regularly checked overnight by detention staff.
Around 7: 50 a.m. the following day, Morissette was found dead in his cell.
An autopsy was conducted and a preliminary police investigation uncovered no evidence of foul play.
Saskatoon lawyer Robert Kennedy will preside as coroner at the inquest, which is scheduled to be heard by a six-member jury from Sept. 8 to 12 at the Sandman Hotel in Saskatoon.
